title: One of the old town’s first streets, end to end
description: The Historical Belfast podcast explores North Street, one of the old town’s original thoroughfares, running from the city centre past the Cathedral Quarter, the arts and nightlife district around St Anne’s Cathedral.

title: A German-born linen baron is hounded out of the city he served
episode: [Documentary] Sir Otto Jaffe: The Linen Entrepreneur Who…
spotify: Best Of Belfast [Documentary] Sir Otto Jaffe: The Linen Entrepreneur Who…
description: Sir Otto Jaffe, a German-Jewish linen merchant, was twice Lord Mayor of Belfast and built its synagogue, yet anti-German feeling in the First World War drove him out. His family’s memorial fountain now stands in Victoria Square.

title: The biggest ship in the world takes shape on the Lagan
spotify: The Rest is History Titanic: The Tragedy Begins (Part 1)
description: Historians Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook begin their series on the Titanic, built from 1909 to 1911 at Harland & Wolff shipyard. Its slipway on Queen’s Island now lies beside the Titanic Belfast museum.

title: Unionist leaders gather at a mansion to defy Home Rule
episode: Craigavon House, with Carol Walker MBE
spotify: Historical Belfast Craigavon House, with Carol Walker MBE
description: Craigavon House in east Belfast, home of unionist leader James Craig, was where Edward Carson rallied crowds against Irish Home Rule in 1911 and where loyalist volunteers drilled. Carol Walker of the Somme Association tells its story.

title: A Catholic family is murdered in their home in 1922
episode: The McMahon Murders, with Edward Burke
spotify: Historical Belfast The McMahon Murders, with Edward Burke
description: In March 1922, amid the violence that followed Ireland’s partition, gunmen broke into publican Owen McMahon’s house on Kinnaird Terrace off the Antrim Road and killed six men. Historian Edward Burke examines who was behind it.

title: Victorian Belfast laid out for the dead, divided underground
episode: Belfast City Cemetery, with Tom Hartley
spotify: Historical Belfast Belfast City Cemetery, with Tom Hartley
description: Tom Hartley, a former Lord Mayor and author of a history of Belfast City Cemetery on the Falls Road, walks its graves of linen barons, shipbuilders and the poor, and the sunken wall said to separate Catholic and Protestant plots.

title: German bombers find a city with almost no shelters
spotify: Dan Snow's History Hit The Belfast Blitz
description: German raids in April and May 1941 killed about 1,000 people in Belfast; the Easter Tuesday raid alone was the deadliest night outside London. Historian Dan Snow covers the attacks, which hit north Belfast’s terraces and mills around York Street.

title: Walls built as a stopgap in 1969 are still standing
description: Belfast’s “peace lines” are barriers between Catholic and Protestant streets, first put up after rioting burned Bombay Street in 1969. Roman Mars’s design show 99% Invisible asks why there are more of them now than in 1998.

title: Twenty IRA bombs go off in an afternoon
episode: Belfast: Bloody Friday – What impact did the IRA’s blitz have…
spotify: The BelTel Belfast: Bloody Friday – What impact did the IRA’s blitz have…
description: On 21 July 1972, during the Troubles (the 30-year conflict over Northern Ireland’s status), the IRA set off about 20 bombs across Belfast in 75 minutes, killing nine. The Belfast Telegraph’s podcast revisits the day and the Oxford Street bus station blast.

title: A record-shop owner gives Belfast punk somewhere to go
episode: Terri Hooley - 75 Revolutions, with Stuart Bailie
place: Good Vibrations record shop, Great Victoria Street
spotify: Historical Belfast Terri Hooley - 75 Revolutions, with Stuart Bailie
description: Terri Hooley opened the Good Vibrations record shop and label in 1976 and released the Undertones’ “Teenage Kicks.” Music writer Stuart Bailie talks about Hooley’s life, and the punk scene that crossed sectarian lines at the height of the Troubles.

title: A gunman attacks mourners at an IRA funeral
spotify: Witness History The Milltown Cemetery attack
description: In March 1988, loyalist Michael Stone threw grenades and fired into the crowd at the funeral of three IRA members in Milltown Cemetery on the Falls Road, killing three. BBC Witness History hears from people who were there.

title: A Nobel poet’s Belfast years at Queen’s
spotify: Frank Skinner's Poetry Podcast Seamus Heaney
description: Comedian Frank Skinner reads and talks through poems by Seamus Heaney, who studied English at Queen’s University Belfast in the 1950s, taught there and joined the Belfast Group of writers before moving south in 1972.

title: Women talk their way into the peace negotiations
episode: Monica McWilliams’ role in the Northern Ireland peace process
spotify: Witness History Monica McWilliams’ role in the Northern Ireland peace process
description: Academic Monica McWilliams co-founded the Northern Ireland Women’s Coalition in 1996, won seats at the peace talks and helped write the 1998 agreement. She went on to sit in the Assembly at Parliament Buildings on the Stormont estate.

title: A deal is struck on Good Friday 1998
spotify: Witness History The Good Friday Agreement
description: After all-night talks at Castle Buildings on the Stormont estate, most of Northern Ireland’s parties and the British and Irish governments approved the Good Friday Agreement on 10 April 1998, the deal that largely ended the Troubles.

title: The man at the door of Europe’s most-bombed hotel
episode: #235 Martin Mullholland: Head Concierge of the…
spotify: Best Of Belfast #235 Martin Mullholland: Head Concierge of the…
description: Martin Mulholland, longtime head concierge of the Europa Hotel on Great Victoria Street, talks about decades at a hotel bombed some 30 times in the Troubles, where journalists, presidents and celebrities have stayed.
